summary: T7-01 passes. I ran all four story checks and each exited cleanly. I judged the six acceptance criteria from the changed files and command output. All changed paths are inside the story's files list, plus `apps/web/components/` added to tsconfig include. I found no blocker or high issues. I did not run the contrast test file or the `.next` CSS output separately. The WCAG numbers and the no-red claim rest on `tests/theme.test.ts` passing (14 tests), not on my own calculation.

findings.claim: cn is the only class-merge helper, and it comes from the less common `cn` package rather than clsx and tailwind-merge.
findings.evidence: apps/web/node_modules/cn/package.json lists repository github.com/shadcn-ui/cn, MIT, and the comment cites shadcn 4.x. This is a pinned exact version and is acceptable. Optionally confirm that dependency choice at merge.

resolution.reason: This is the dependency shadcn/ui itself ships for the chosen style. The registry item https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/radix-nova/utils.json (fetched 2026-11-14) lists dependencies ["cn"], and its lib/utils.ts is exactly `export { cn } from "cn"`, which apps/web/lib/utils.ts reproduces. The package is published from github.com/shadcn-ui/cn (MIT; apps/web/node_modules/cn/package.json), describes itself as a drop-in replacement for clsx and tailwind-merge, and is pinned at 0.5.2. tests/ui.test.tsx checks the behaviour the components rely on: falsy values are dropped and the later Tailwind class wins (px-2 then px-4 gives px-4). Swapping in clsx and tailwind-merge would diverge from the registry that components.json points at. The finding itself rates the choice acceptable, so no change is needed.

findings.claim: Two Button/Badge classes (`disabled:opacity-50` and the 80%-opacity hover) could fall below AA contrast when shown. Disabled controls are exempt from WCAG contrast, and the hover state is not covered by a contrast test I saw.
findings.evidence: button.tsx:16 and :20 (`hover:bg-primary/80`). Nothing renders these components yet, so there is no current impact.

resolution.reason: Hover and expanded states are now covered by a contrast test that derives colours from the variant classes, not a hand-kept list. tests/variant-colours.ts reads each Button and Badge variant at rest, under hover:, [a]:hover: and aria-expanded:, and in every combination of those states. Translucent fills such as hover:bg-primary/80 are composited in sRGB over each page surface (background, secondary, muted, accent) with the new composite() in tests/contrast.ts. Each case must reach 4.5:1. The 80% primary hover measures 9.19:1 on --background, 9.48:1 on --secondary/--muted and 9.92:1 on --accent, so no component class needed to change. A class the model cannot judge (opacity outside disabled:, arbitrary or non-token colours, gradients) throws instead of being skipped. Changing the Button hover to bg-primary/30 made the test fail at 1.88:1 (checked, then reverted). The disabled:opacity-50 part needs no change: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 sets no contrast requirement for text in an inactive user interface component, so the disabled state is skipped explicitly. Failing tests first in 2f5ee6b.
